A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, renamed from S4D to H3D-DGS. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices, including image-only pages, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original Neu3DV and CMU-Panoptic reconstruction results, motion-component ablations, optical-flow comparisons, and control-point pruning results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports additional baseline comparisons in Tables 2–3 and Figure 5.

M1.justification: Both use optical-flow-derived observable motion, three learnable motion components, inverse-distance control-point interpolation, object segmentation, and keyframe residual updates with the same reconstruction loss. Renaming the representation and disclosing sampling settings do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both evaluate multiview dynamic reconstruction on the same six Neu3DV sequences and three CMU-Panoptic sequences. Changes to qualitative examples and comparator participation do not introduce another dataset, task, or domain.

E2.justification: v2 compares reconstruction against Dynamic-GS and 4D-GS. v3 adds MA-GS and SP-GS throughout the Neu3DV quantitative comparison, plus SC-GS results for two scenes and qualitative comparisons. Tables 2–3 and Figure 5 therefore substantially expand the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 reverses the reported camera arrangements: Neu3DV changes from spherical to fanned, and CMU-Panoptic from fanned to spherical. This revises stated settings without establishing changed data or reruns. Resolutions, sequence lengths, the CMU split, and 10k/500/100-iteration budgets remain unchanged; Appendix A.6 specifies the deformation-based MA-GS pipeline for its new comparison.

E4.justification: The coffee_martini qualitative comparison is expanded with SP-GS and SC-GS outputs, while the final qualitative example on v2's page 20 is omitted. The motion-component ablation, pruning study, optical-flow sensitivity comparison, initial-frame correlation, and motion visualizations are retained, often relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds MA-GS/SP-GS averages, including 28.76/27.03 dB PSNR, their per-scene results, and two SC-GS result rows. Shared reconstruction scores remain unchanged. Reported keyframe time changes from approximately 40 to 10 seconds, and control-point accounting changes from 3 attributes and 0.6–7.5k parameters to 9 attributes and 1.8–22.5k parameters. These substantially extend comparative evidence without showing improved reconstruction scores for the retained method.

T1.justification: The projection and interpolation reasoning and the near-parallel-ray proof, including Appendix Equations 12–14, remain equivalent. Explicit quaternion conversion and Gaussian-update equations unpack operations already described in v2; coordinate and notation refinements do not introduce new mathematical results.

C1.justification: Despite the new title and heterogeneous terminology, both retain the central contributions: observable/learned motion decomposition, compact control points, streaming Gaussian reconstruction, superior results on the same datasets, and the 100-iteration/about-two-second optimization headline.

C2.justification: v3 expands the coffee_martini interpretation by distinguishing background-related metric errors from dynamic-region detail. Its conclusion adds background floaters and jitter as limitations, attributing them to sequential noise accumulation and temporal drift. Initialization dependence and the lack of monocular support remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies K=3 and sampling interval/radius settings of 64/16 pixels for Neu3DV and 32/8 for CMU-Panoptic. It explicitly identifies DIS as the default optical-flow method and documents implementation choices for the added comparators. These are additional disclosures rather than demonstrated changes to the retained experiments.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially refocused around control-point methods and the distinction between structural motion constraints and fully gradient-based estimation. v3 adds a capability matrix and detailed positioning against MA-GS, SP-GS, and SC-GS, incorporates works such as MotionGS and Spacetime Gaussian, and removes much of the earlier static-NeRF acceleration survey.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and method exposition are extensively rewritten. The method changes from a workflow-first organization to notation and motion decoupling first. Segmentation and residual compensation are condensed, pruning subsections are merged, and analyses are reorganized between the main text and appendix.

P2.justification: v3 adds a teaser figure and capability table, redraws control-point and prior-acquisition diagrams, adds a grid-sampling panel, and restructures benchmark tables and qualitative comparisons. Motion tracks and initial-quality plots move to the appendix, while the optical-flow table moves into the main text. These are extensive display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: Additional comparisons against relevant control-point methods, explicit sampling settings, clearer method exposition, and the background-jitter limitation improve the paper's assessability and reproducibility. The gain is tempered by unexplained numerical presentation: v3 Figure 1 gives SP-GS PSNR/SSIM as 27.58/0.9158, whereas Table 2 gives 27.03/0.9109. The core method and matched reconstruction results remain stable.
